intro.title: kube-sched-advisor
lines: Describe a workload in plain English. Get a scheduling plan from your live cluster.
Recorded on a real Amazon EKS cluster. No narration: each step has a caption.
4 real NVIDIA A10G GPUs, plus 3 stand-in nodes that advertise 8 GPUs each but have none.
Every node is labelled real or stand-in on screen.

steps.caption: Seven GPU nodes. Four have one real A10G each. Three are stand-ins: CPU machines that advertise 8 GPUs and have none.
steps.command: kubectl get nodes -l nvidia.com/gpu.product -o custom-columns='NODE:.metadata.name,KIND:.metadata.labels.ksa/gpu-kind,TYPE:.metadata.labels.node\.kubernetes\.io/instance-type,GPUS:.status.allocatable.nvidia\.com/gpu,GPU-PRODUCT:.metadata.labels.nvidia\.com/gpu\.product'
steps.output:
NODE                                           KIND       TYPE        GPUS   GPU-PRODUCT
gpu-node-1                                     real       g5.xlarge   1      NVIDIA-A10G
standin-node-1                                 stand-in   t3.medium   8      NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3
standin-node-2                                 stand-in   t3.medium   8      NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3
gpu-node-2                                     real       g5.xlarge   1      NVIDIA-A10G
gpu-node-3                                     real       g5.xlarge   1      NVIDIA-A10G
standin-node-3                                 stand-in   t3.medium   8      NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3
gpu-node-4                                     real       g5.xlarge   1      NVIDIA-A10G

section.title: The cluster
section.subtitle: 4 real A10G GPUs, plus 3 stand-in nodes. Every node is labelled.

steps.caption: Other teams run jobs on both kinds of node: 1 GPU on two real nodes, and 2 of the 8 stand-in GPUs on each stand-in node.
steps.command: kubectl get pods -n other-teams -o custom-columns='POD:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName,GPUS-HELD:.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.nvidia\.com/gpu'
steps.output:
POD                  NODE                                           GPUS-HELD
other-team-a         gpu-node-1                                     1
other-team-b         gpu-node-2                                     1
standin-team-job-0   standin-node-1                                 2
standin-team-job-1   standin-node-2                                 2
standin-team-job-2   standin-node-3                                 2

steps.caption: The advisor reads the live cluster through kubectl. Nothing is changed.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor status
steps.output:
Kubernetes 1.37 on EKS
Installed add-ons: none
Network topology label: network.topology/block
Node pools:
- 2x NVIDIA-A10G (NVIDIA-A10G) in us-east-2b: 1 GPU/node, 0 GPUs free, 0 fully-free nodes, 7.3 CPU free, taints=['nvidia.com/gpu']
- 1x NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3 (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3) in us-east-2b: 8 GPU/node, 6 GPUs free, 0 fully-free nodes, 1.765 CPU free, taints=none
- 1x NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3 (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3) in us-east-2a: 8 GPU/node, 6 GPUs free, 0 fully-free nodes, 1.765 CPU free, taints=none
- 2x NVIDIA-A10G (NVIDIA-A10G) in us-east-2c: 1 GPU/node, 2 GPUs free, 2 fully-free nodes, 7.23 CPU free, taints=['nvidia.com/gpu']
- 1x NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3 (NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3) in us-east-2c: 8 GPU/node, 6 GPUs free, 0 fully-free nodes, 1.765 CPU free, taints=none

steps.caption: The ask, in plain English. The advisor warns that starting 2 of 3 workers would deadlock the job.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor suggest --brief --name gang-train --image nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 --command "nvidia-smi -L" "train on 3 workers, 1 A10G GPU each, all-or-nothing, 1 cpu and 1 GiB per pod"
steps.output:
Recommended: Secondary scheduler gang-scheduler (scheduler-plugins Coscheduling + GPU bin-packing)

Why:
  - Pin to nvidia.com/gpu.product=NVIDIA-A10G so the pod only lands on A10G nodes.
  - Add tolerations for GPU-node taints (taints keep CPU pods off GPUs; a toleration only allows
    placement, it does not attract the pod - the nodeSelector/requests do that).
  - No batch system is installed, so the lightest gang option is the Coscheduling plugin from
    kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins.
  - It runs as a second scheduler: the default scheduler is untouched (required on EKS, where the
    default scheduler's config cannot be edited).

Findings:
  BLOCKER: Not enough free GPUs right now.
  WARNING: The gang cannot start right now under any scoring strategy.
  WARNING: Partial placement would deadlock the job.
  NOTE: Coscheduling does not wake up when GPUs free up.
  NOTE: EKS: default scheduler config is not editable.

Simulation: default scheduler places 2/3 pods; 2 GPUs free, 2 whole nodes free

Manifests and the full report: out/gang-train/

section.title: Scenario 1: a training job that must start all at once (real GPUs)
section.subtitle: Real GPUs. 3 workers, 1 GPU each. Only 2 real GPUs are free.

steps.caption: The same job on the default scheduler, for real: two workers start and hold GPUs. The third waits.
steps.command: kubectl apply -f demo/plain-job.yaml && sleep 15 && kubectl get pods -l job-name=plain-train -o custom-columns='POD:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,NODE:.spec.nodeName'
steps.output:
job.batch/plain-train created
POD                 STATUS    NODE
plain-train-bcmn2   Running   gpu-node-4                                  
plain-train-tmj5n   Running   gpu-node-3                                  
plain-train-tp9qp   Pending   <none>

steps.caption: Delete it. Those two GPUs were held for a job that could never finish.
steps.command: kubectl delete job plain-train --wait=true
steps.output: job.batch "plain-train" deleted from default namespace

steps.caption: Apply what the advisor generated: a second scheduler with the Coscheduling plugin, and a PodGroup for the job.

steps.caption: Submit the job. All three workers wait, and none holds a GPU. Two are free, three are needed.
steps.command: kubectl apply -f out/gang-train/30-workload.yaml && sleep 25 && kubectl get pods -n research -o custom-columns='POD:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,NODE:.spec.nodeName'
steps.output:

POD                  STATUS    NODE

gang-train-1-nwhnf   Pending   <none>
gang-train-2-cgqmf   Pending   <none>

steps.caption: Another team's job finishes and frees one GPU.
steps.command: kubectl delete pod -n other-teams other-team-b
steps.output: pod "other-team-b" deleted from other-teams namespace

steps.caption: The gang scheduler retries on new pods and on a 5-minute timer, not when a GPU frees up. Still waiting.
steps.command: sleep 20 && kubectl get pods -n research -o custom-columns='POD:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,NODE:.spec.nodeName'
steps.output:
POD                  STATUS    NODE
gang-train-0-xfjlp   Pending   <none>
gang-train-1-nwhnf   Pending   <none>
gang-train-2-cgqmf   Pending   <none>

steps.caption: As the advisor's note says: touch the PodGroup and the scheduler retries at once.
steps.command: kubectl annotate podgroup -n research gang-train retry=$(date +%s) --overwrite
steps.output: podgroup.scheduling.x-k8s.io/gang-train annotated

steps.caption: All three workers start together, each on its own real GPU.
steps.command: kubectl wait --for=condition=complete job/gang-train -n research --timeout=300s && kubectl logs -n research -l job-name=gang-train --prefix
steps.output:
job.batch/gang-train condition met
[pod/gang-train-0-xfjlp/main] GPU 0: NVIDIA A10G (UUID: GPU-<id>)
[pod/gang-train-1-nwhnf/main] GPU 0: NVIDIA A10G (UUID: GPU-<id>)
[pod/gang-train-2-cgqmf/main] GPU 0: NVIDIA A10G (UUID: GPU-<id>)

steps.caption: A serving ask. No gang scheduler this time: the default scheduler, zone spread and a disruption budget.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor suggest --brief --name gpu-serve --image nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 --command "sleep infinity" "serve a chat model, 2 replicas, 1 A10G GPU each, highly available, 1 cpu and 1 GiB per pod"
steps.output:
Recommended: Default kube-scheduler + spreading (Deployment, topology spread, PDB)

Why:
  - Pin to nvidia.com/gpu.product=NVIDIA-A10G so the pod only lands on A10G nodes.
  - Add tolerations for GPU-node taints (taints keep CPU pods off GPUs; a toleration only allows
    placement, it does not attract the pod - the nodeSelector/requests do that).
  - Serving needs availability, not packing: keep the default LeastAllocated scoring so replicas
    spread out and a single node failure costs one replica.
  - Topology spread across topology.kubernetes.io/zone is hard (DoNotSchedule) because this is
    critical.
  - A PodDisruptionBudget keeps node drains/Karpenter consolidation from taking out several replicas
    at once.

Simulation: default scheduler places 2/2 pods; 3 GPUs free, 3 whole nodes free

Manifests and the full report: out/gpu-serve/

section.title: Scenario 2: a highly available inference service (real GPUs)
section.subtitle: 2 replicas, 1 GPU each. A different ask gets a different plan, applied for real.

steps.caption: Apply the generated manifests for real. The only edits are the image and command given on the command line.
steps.command: kubectl apply -f out/gpu-serve/00-priorityclass.yaml -f out/gpu-serve/30-workload.yaml && kubectl rollout status -n research deploy/gpu-serve --timeout=300s
steps.output:

steps.caption: The ask: 2 nodes with 8 H100 GPUs each. Other teams hold 2 stand-in GPUs on every node, so 18 are free but no node has 8.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor suggest --brief --name gang-big "2 nodes x 8 H100 GPUs per node, NVLink, all-or-nothing fine-tune, 1 cpu and 1 GiB per pod"
steps.output:
Recommended: Secondary scheduler gang-scheduler (scheduler-plugins Coscheduling + GPU bin-packing)

Why:
  - Pin to nvidia.com/gpu.product=NVIDIA-H100-80GB-HBM3 so the pod only lands on H100 nodes.
  - Add tolerations for GPU-node taints (taints keep CPU pods off GPUs; a toleration only allows
    placement, it does not attract the pod - the nodeSelector/requests do that).
  - No batch system is installed, so the lightest gang option is the Coscheduling plugin from
    kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins.
  - It runs as a second scheduler: the default scheduler is untouched (required on EKS, where the
    default scheduler's config cannot be edited).

Findings:
  BLOCKER: No node can run even one pod.
  WARNING: Enough GPUs in total, but they are fragmented.
  WARNING: The gang cannot start right now under any scoring strategy.
  WARNING: No single network domain can host the whole job.
  NOTE: Coscheduling does not wake up when GPUs free up.
  NOTE: EKS: default scheduler config is not editable.

Simulation: default scheduler places 0/2 pods; no single network.topology/block has room for the
            whole job; 18 GPUs free, 0 whole nodes free

Manifests and the full report: out/gang-big/

section.title: Scenario 4: asking for hardware the cluster does not have
section.subtitle: The advisor should say so instead of generating a job that never starts.

steps.caption: Kueue is installed on the cluster. The advisor detects it from the cluster's API extensions.
steps.command: kubectl get pods -n kueue-system && kubectl get crd clusterqueues.kueue.x-k8s.io
steps.output:

kueue-controller-manager-5f58576dcf-km4sv   1/1     Running   0          17s

section.title: Scenario 5: the platform team installs Kueue
section.subtitle: The advisor notices and changes its plan.

steps.caption: A shared-pool ask on the same cluster. The plan now uses Kueue queues.
steps.command: python -m sched_advisor suggest --brief --name gang-kueue "train on 3 workers, 1 A10G GPU each, all-or-nothing, shared pool with other teams, 1 cpu and 1 GiB per pod"
steps.output:
Recommended: Kueue admission (all-or-nothing quota) + gpu-binpack bin-packing profile

Why:
  - Pin to nvidia.com/gpu.product=NVIDIA-A10G so the pod only lands on A10G nodes.
  - Add tolerations for GPU-node taints (taints keep CPU pods off GPUs; a toleration only allows
    placement, it does not attract the pod - the nodeSelector/requests do that).
  - Kueue keeps the Job suspended until quota for all workers is available, then admits it as a
    unit.
  - A ClusterQueue per team inside a shared cohort gives fair sharing: idle quota is borrowable and
    reclaimed with preemption when its owner needs it back.
  - gpu-binpack uses MostAllocated with nvidia.com/gpu weight 5: fill GPU nodes before touching
    empty ones, so whole nodes stay free for big jobs and idle nodes can be scaled down.

Findings:
  BLOCKER: Not enough free GPUs right now.
  WARNING: The gang cannot start right now under any scoring strategy.
  WARNING: Partial placement would deadlock the job.
  NOTE: EKS: default scheduler config is not editable.

Simulation: default scheduler places 1/3 pods; 1 GPUs free, 1 whole nodes free

Manifests and the full report: out/gang-kueue/
